title: SRS resumes shipments of remote-handled transuranic waste to WIPP
summary: A new type of heavy-duty shielded container is being used to ship remote-handled legacy transuranic waste from the Savannah River Site in Aiken, S.C., to the Waste Isolation Pilot Plant in New Mexico. The Department of Energy’s Office of Environmental Management announced this week that the first shipment using the new packaging was successfully completed.

title: Zaporizhzhia restores off-site power following IAEA-brokered local ceasefire
summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency brokered a temporary ceasefire in and around Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia plant that allowed key repairs at the Russian-occupied nuclear power plant to be carried out, the organization announced Saturday. Workers began repairing a damaged power line north of the Dnipro River, the IAEA update said. Those repairs, completed earlier this week, restored off-site power to Zaporizhzhia, which had been running on emergency diesel generators. On Monday, plant operator Energoatom said on Facebook that the plant was receiving external power again after Ukrainian workers restored the 330-kV Ferosplavna-1 line.

title: IAEA continues inspection activities in post-Assad Syria
summary: According to a report by the Associated Press, inspectors with the International Atomic Energy Agency have confirmed that Syria under the leadership of President Bashar Assad, who was ousted amid civil conflict in 2024, was building a nuclear reactor in the eastern Syrian city of Deir ez Zor. The IAEA inspectors visited that site in August, following up on a previous inspection that had detected uranium in samples taken there.

title: Improve your home’s energy efficiency with Entergy Mississippi’s READI program
summary: Entergy Mississippi’s READI Program offers homeowners a simple way to save energy and money. Schedule a walk-through, get a personalized report, and enjoy instant installation of energy-saving products. Upgrades like duct sealing and insulation may also be available. Source

title: Entergy volunteers help move Capitol Green Connector project forward
summary: Volunteers—including Entergy employees—helped plant trees and landscaping along the Capitol Green Connector, making downtown Jackson greener and more welcoming. Supported by local organizations, the project extends the Museum Trail and connects key destinations. Source

title: Stay alert: Utility customers being targeted with new QR and barcode scams
